More than 100 aftershocks as high as magnitude-5.8 recorded after two quakes toppled buildings and prompted evacuations

Panama’s government has declared a state of emergency on Saturday as the aftershocks of two powerful earthquakes that roiled the country shook communities for hours.

Officials did not attribute any deaths to Friday’s 7.7- and 6.6-magnitude earthquakes, but reported damages in all 10 of Panama’s provinces and two Indigenous territories.

guardian.description:
Leftwing Hitler Mussolini Simeon Flores beats far-right candidate in election in remote district of Andes

A businessman called Hitler Mussolini Simeon Flores has been elected the mayor of a remote district in the Peruvian Andes, according to local election data.

The 45-year-old, who shares two of his names with the notorious European dictators, won the race for mayor of Queropalca, in Peru’s central Huánuco region, and will take office on 1 January.

Oliver Blume said “Made in Europe” rules from the EU “must reward real value creation in Europe”, speaking in Paris before the motor show this week.

rfi.title: France urges Palestinians to reverse decision on delayed elections
rfi.description: France on Sunday called on Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas to reverse a decision to postpone legislative elections, originally set for 28 November. Abbas said on Saturday that due to "Israeli obstacles", the vote would be held in September next year, alongside a presidential poll.

rfi.title: Western leaders slam Houthi attack on Riyadh airport, warn citizens to stay away
rfi.description: UN and EU leaders voiced shock and anger on Sunday following an attack by Yemen's Houthi rebels on Riyadh airport in Saudi Arabia and warned against an escalation in the deadly conflict. Several embassies have issued warnings to their citizens to avoid the area.

rfi.title: Rescuers search for missing migrants after deadly boat wreck off Djibouti
rfi.description: The death toll from a boat sinking off the shores of Djibouti on the night of 8-9 October, has risen to at least 139, a UN agency said Sunday, after 30 more bodies were found. Rescue operations are underway to find the dozens of missing. More than 80 people survived the shipwreck, all Ethiopian nationals.

rfi.title: Climate lawsuits gain ground as governments scale back climate action
rfi.description: The political fight against global warming may be losing steam, but the legal battle is heating up. Over the past decade, legal activists have successfully taken a number of national governments to court, triggering the adoption of more climate-friendly policies in countries including the Netherlands, Pakistan, Switzerland, South Korea and others.

rfi.title: How Egyptian femtech is tackling taboos around women's health
rfi.description: Cultural taboos and a lack of understanding can be a barrier for women to access healthcare in Egypt, alongside the cost of treatment. But the country's budding femtech sector is creating new pathways to help and inform.

rfi.title: Palestinian Mahmoud Abu Hamda wins top photography prize at Bayeux
rfi.description: Palestinian freelancer Mahmoud Abu Hamda on Saturday won the photography category in the prestigious Bayeux award for war correspondents for his work from Gaza.

rfi.title: France boss Zidane generates 'electric atmosphere' with Nations League wins
rfi.description: Zinédine Zidane was renowned for his prodigious skills during a 17-year playing career that took him from the streets of Marseille to glamorous European clubs such as Juventus and Real Madrid – as well as to a World Cup win for France in 1998. Now, as France coach, he is showing that his flair for the unexpected has not deserted him.

rfi.title: French prodigy Seixas becomes youngest Giro di Lombardia winner
rfi.description: French cycling prodigy Paul Seixas ended his breakout season as a history-making Monument winner with a "dream" victory at the Giro di Lombardia on Saturday at just 20 years old.

rfi.title: EU says US deal lifting diesel sanctions 'funds' Russian war on Ukraine
rfi.description: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Saturday that lifting sanctions on Russian diesel helped fuel the Kremlin's war on Ukraine, after US President Donald Trump announced a deal for Moscow to supply fuel.

rfi.title: French Socialist party primary vote extended due to cyberattack
rfi.description: The first round of France's Socialist Party's primary has been extended until 6pm on Sunday after a cyberattack slowed down proceedings, organisers said. An investigation is underway.

rfi.title: French astronaut recounts 'astonishing' emotions after return to Earth
rfi.description: French astronaut Sophie Adenot has returned back to earth full of "emotion" after spending eight months in space – breaking the record for the longest uninterrupted orbital stay by a European astronaut. She will complete a recovery programme at the European Space Agency centre in Cologne, Germany before returning to France.

rfi.title: France promises more teachers and student representation but protests continue
rfi.description: France's government has promised 3,000 replacement teachers for struggling secondary schools and pledged to give pupils a greater say in education policy in a bid to quell nearly three weeks of student protests. But blockades in some schools resumed on Friday morning and student bodies have called for a further day of action next week.

rfi.title: Exiled Ukrainian women prepare for life after war, with or without returning home
rfi.description: Since the full-scale Russian invasion on February 2022, Ukrainian organisations abroad have taken on an increasingly important role in supporting their country. With women and children making up the majority of recent exiles, women's groups have a particular part to play in winning support for Ukraine – as well as making sure its cultural identity survives.

rfi.title: UN alarmed as number of displaced in central Sahel reaches nearly four million
rfi.description: The United Nations on Friday raised the alarm about a displacement crisis in the central Sahel where nearly four million people have been forced to flee their homes in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger.

rfi.title: Ghana faces challenge to persuade Brics it deserves a seat at the table
rfi.description: Ghana is seeking to widen its trade and diplomatic options beyond the West by applying to join the Brics bloc of emerging economies. But a seat at the table is far from guaranteed: Ghana will have to convince all 11 existing members it is a valuable new partner.

rfi.title: A race against time to prevent an outbreak follows Kenya's first Ebola death
rfi.description: Kenya's first imported case of Ebola – in which the patient travelled from Democratic Republic of Congo via Uganda – has exposed failings in border screening processes. Now Kenyan health officials are racing against the clock to prevent one infection from becoming an outbreak.

rfi.title: Houthi war risks dragging Israel and Turkey into Horn of Africa standoff
rfi.description: The escalating clash between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia now threatens to ignite the already tense rivalry between Israel and Turkey in the Horn of Africa. This week, Turkey threw its military weight behind Saudi Arabia, while Somaliland – a self-declared state recognised only by Israel – is urgently seeking Israeli military support.

rfi.title: Niger intelligence agents expelled from France in sign of diplomatic strain
rfi.description: Two Nigerien intelligence officers were forced to leave France last month, French daily Le Monde has revealed, with one agent suspected of monitoring opposition figures on French soil. It is the latest sign of the deterioration in relations between the two countries since Niger’s 2023 military coup.

euronews.title: Shakira sets Amazon Music record in Madrid with most-watched live stream by a female artist
euronews.description: The global broadcast of the Colombian singer's Madrid concert has become the most-watched live performance by a female artist on Amazon Music. The platform highlights the role of the Spanish capital as a bridge between Latin America and Europe.

euronews.title: Antarctic penguins emit up to 7 million tonnes of methane a year, study finds
euronews.description: A study by CSIC and the University of Granada finds that chinstrap penguin colonies are a previously unmeasured natural source of methane, emitting up to 7 million tonnes a year.

euronews.title: French Social democratic primary: Raphaël Glucksmann wins big in first round
euronews.description: With more than 66% in the primary, French MEP Raphaël Glucksmann is chosen as the social-democratic candidate for France’s 2027 presidential election. On X, he insists that "a left true to its values can unite, govern and win".

euronews.title: Nepal orders evacuations after landslide triggers Budhi Gandaki flash flood
euronews.description: Nepal’s authorities ordered residents along the Budhi Gandaki River to evacuate on Sunday, 11 October, after a sudden flash flood swept away homes and other buildings in the country’s mountainous north-central region.

euronews.title: Ten of thousands urge EU for climate action at Brussels demonstration
euronews.description: Ahead of a major UN summit, thousands of protesters marched through the streets of Brussels demanding greater action to combat climate change.

euronews.title: Police clear Guano beach camp in Ceuta days before royal visit
euronews.description: Spain's National Police have cleared Guano beach in Ceuta, where about 400 migrants were still camped, two days before the King and Queen visit the city. It was the last remaining camp; some migrants fled to the nearby hills.

euronews.title: Paris motor show: Macron calls for European preference against China
euronews.description: On Monday, the French president will open his final Paris Motor Show, pushing his "Made in Europe" agenda: tying state aid for this key industry to genuinely EU-based production.

euronews.description: Rescuers have been battling to rescue people affected by the flash floods in Nepal that swept 45 houses and left five people missing.

euronews.title: 'Energy ceasefire' agreed between Russia and Ukraine, Trump says
euronews.description: After Donald Trump's criticism blaming Volodymyr Zelenskyy for high diesel prices, suggesting Ukraine should get a new leader, US President announced Russia and Ukraine had agreed on an 'energy ceasefire'.

euronews.title: Hochvogel mountain at risk of major collapse as 400,000 cubic metres of rock threatens to break away
euronews.description: The Hochvogel sits on the border between Germany and the Austrian region of Tyrol. It is part of the Allgäu High Alps and stands at 2,592 metres high.

euronews.title: 'Up to our people' to pick leader, Zelenskyy responds to Trump's pledge for new elections in Ukraine
euronews.description: Only Russia is responsible for the war in Ukraine, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Sunday in a TV interview, responding to criticism from US President Donald Trump, who blamed him for high diesel prices and said he should be replaced.

euronews.title: At least 139 migrants dead after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN says
euronews.description: The UN's IOM agency says tens of thousands of migrants travel from the Horn of Africa through Djibouti each year as they look to cross the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to Yemen and eventually reach the Gulf countries.

euronews.title: Russian army strikes Sloviansk and Kyiv as Ukrainian drones hit third Yandex data centre
euronews.description: Russian forces struck two apartment blocks in Sloviansk, injuring four, and hit warehouses in Kyiv. Overnight, Ukrainian drones targeted Yandex's data centre in Vladimir, causing major service outages but no casualties.

euronews.title: Saudi-led coalition says a projectile has struck a passenger terminal at the airport in Riyadh
euronews.description: Fire was reported after an unidentified projectile hit Riyadh airport terminal less than a day after an attack killed 12 people. The attack led to Riyadh’s airport shutdown and drew condemnation from the UN and EU, as the Houthis renew their threats and Washington considers its response.

euronews.title: Macron's popularity hits lowest level since 2017 as Bardella and Le Pen also lose ground
euronews.description: Some 82% of French people now disapprove of the president. Meanwhile, Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella are weakened by Mediapart's revelations about antisemitic texts attributed to the young RN leader.

euronews.title: Denmark tests humanoid robots in supermarkets to help to ease staff workload at night
euronews.description: Denmark’s Salling Group is trialling Hive Robots in stores to handle demanding restocking, freeing staff for customer service while robots work mainly at night.

euronews.title: Zaporizhzhia airstrikes kill 17 as Russia intensifies attacks across Ukraine
euronews.description: Zaporizhzhia was hit by deadly Russian airstrikes on Saturday, 10 October, killing at least 17 people, including three children, Ukrainian officials said. Rescuers searched rubble for survivors as the city faced renewed strikes on residential areas.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, primaire à gauche : Raphaël Glucksmann affirme que sa victoire est celle de « tous ceux qui croient que la gauche doit rompre » avec LFI et tend la main à François Hollande
lemonde.description: L’eurodéputé a été largement désigné candidat de la gauche sociale-démocrate à la présidentielle, dès le premier tour de la primaire, avec 66 % des voix. Il devance de très loin le premier secrétaire du PS, Olivier Faure (14 %). Ségolène Royal, Jérôme Guedj et Emmanuel Maurel obtiennent tous moins de 10 % des voix.

lemonde.title: Pourquoi Ceuta et Melilla restent un sujet de discorde entre l’Espagne et le Maroc
lemonde.description: L’arrivée de plus de 72 000 migrants à Ceuta, en provenance du Maroc, les 30 et 31 juillet, a ravivé la question de la souveraineté de l’Espagne sur les deux villes autonomes de la côte nord-africaine. Une souveraineté revendiquée par Rabat depuis les années 1960, à laquelle la visite annoncée du roi Felipe VI, le 13 octobre, doit symboliquement opposer une énième fin de non-recevoir.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Volodymyr Zelensky affirme que la Russie a frappé des installations énergétiques après l’annonce par Donald Trump d’un cessez-le-feu énergétique
lemonde.description: Le président américain a assuré que la Russie et l’Ukraine étaient convenues de mettre fin aux frappes contre leurs infrastructures énergétiques respectives.

lemonde.title: Soins « graine », distribution de noisettes et stages de méditation : un ostéopathe guérisseur jugé pour abus de faiblesse à Paris
lemonde.description: Antonino Mercuri, qui se vantait d’avoir soigné François Mitterrand, a accumulé une fortune avec des « soins », déclarant lors de son interpellation des revenus annuels à hauteur de 1,3 million d’euros. Plusieurs de ses clients qui ont dû vendre leurs biens et se sont lourdement endettés refusent d’être considérés comme des victimes.

lemonde.title: Arabie saoudite : les houthistes du Yémen revendiquent des « opérations d’envergure » contres des aéroports et des infrastructures énergétiques
lemonde.description: L’ampleur des attaques visant Riyad ces derniers jours est inédite depuis le début en 2014 de la guerre au Yémen. Elles ont fait 13 morts, samedi, et de très nombreux blessés.

lemonde.title: Avec « L’Architecte de Notre-Dame », Aurélien Bellanger orchestre un grand spectacle de théories
lemonde.description: Autour de deux duos de personnages qui collent mal à leurs époques, l’écrivain signe un roman ambitieux et une stimulante histoire d’histoires.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Jean-Luc Mélenchon promet de supprimer « l’ignominie » Parcoursup devant une salle comble à Clermont-Ferrand
lemonde.description: Le leader « insoumis » a renouvelé, dimanche, ses encouragements appuyés au mouvement de colère lycéen, dont il a loué la « très grande maturité politique et syndicale ».

lemonde.title: Devenir veuve et le rester : « Certaines réussissent à refaire leur vie. Mais ça se compte sur les doigts d’une main »
lemonde.description: Passé 60 ans, le veuvage concerne majoritairement les femmes et dure en moyenne plus de dix ans. Est-il équivalent de solitude, choisie ou subie ? Comment ces années s’étirent-elles ? Quatre femmes, de 76 à 96 ans, témoignent.

lemonde.description: L’homme qui menaçait de commettre cette attaque a été arrêté, ont annoncé le premier ministre et le ministre de l’intérieur. « Nous traitons cette affaire avec le plus grand sérieux », a commenté le porte-parole du ministre-coordinateur des services spéciaux.

lemonde.title: Derrière le site complotiste Géopolitique profonde, plagiat, IA et sous-traitance à Madagascar
lemonde.description: Ce site majeur de la complosphère française fait appel à des rédacteurs malgaches pour copier-coller des articles trouvés sur Internet et les soumettre à une intelligence artificielle chargée de leur donner une tonalité « plutôt pro-droite, pro-Trump, pro-Poutine, anti-UE ».

lemonde.title: Au Canada, l’armée confrontée à la difficile défense de l’immense territoire arctique
lemonde.description: Loin de la démonstration de force promise, l’opération « Nanook-Nunakput », menée en septembre dans le Grand Nord par l’armée canadienne, a surtout mis en lumière la complexe protection d’un territoire grand comme l’Union européenne, pourtant au cœur des ambitions stratégiques d’Ottawa.

lemonde.title: Egalité et réconciliation, l’association d’extrême droite fondée par Alain Soral, visée par une procédure de dissolution
lemonde.description: Le ministère de l’intérieur soutient que l’association, sous couvert de « combattre le racisme ou d’assister les victimes de discrimination fondée sur leur origine nationale, ethnique, raciale ou religieuse », « reprend en réalité le courant [de] pensée national-socialiste, référence directe au nazisme ».

lemonde.title: Manchester City dispose de Liverpool et s’envole en tête de la Premier League
lemonde.description: Les Mancuniens se sont imposés, dimanche à Anfield, face à Liverpool (3-0), au terme d’un match intense, et comptent trois points d’avance sur Arsenal, leur dauphin. Les Reds restent, eux, englués dans le milieu du classement.

lemonde.title: Trieste, le port qui ne se savait pas italien
lemonde.description: Sous la protection de la maison de Habsbourg depuis le XIVe siècle, Trieste est, à la veille de la première guerre mondiale, la troisième ville d’Autriche. Si les Habsbourg avaient été à l’origine de la fortune du petit port sur l’Adriatique, leur chute causera sa perte.

lemonde.title: Porsche, toujours plus chère et plus sportive pour une clientèle de passionnés

It is also due to deep evolutionary roots, as many animal and plant groups originated here in the distant past. Paleontologists have been excavating this material for nearly two centuries.

These atomic-scale defects can give diamonds new optical and electronic properties, and some of them can serve as quantum systems. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

proj-syn.title: A Global Economic Recovery Built on Shaky Foundations
proj-syn.description: The latest update of the Brookings-FT TIGER survey reveals that global growth has stabilized, with both advanced and emerging market economies showing positive momentum. But amid persistent inflation and fiscal profligacy, policymakers will still be forced to push forward with structural reforms to unleash productivity growth.

proj-syn.title: The French Far Right Embraces Austerity
proj-syn.description: In a recent speech detailing her economic program, the French far-right leader Marine Le Pen offered what can only be described as a populist vision of fiscal consolidation. Whether she can make such a paradoxical formulation work will now determine her own future, and possibly that of Europe’s nationalist right.

proj-syn.title: Rating Africa on Its Own Terms
proj-syn.description: For decades, African countries' borrowing costs have been largely determined by major credit-rating agencies whose methods overlook key features of these economies' institutions and markets. The new Africa Credit Rating Agency could mark a turning point, challenging how the continent’s credit risk is graded and priced.

proj-syn.title: Development Finance Needs More Than One Currency
proj-syn.description: For many developing countries, renminbi-denominated loans offer a credible, increasingly accessible, and cost-effective alternative to borrowing in dollars. Now that the stability and predictability of US economic policies and institutions are in question, the Chinese currency is becoming more attractive.

proj-syn.title: Mélenchon Is Right About France’s Debt
proj-syn.description: When, in the name of moderation, centrists brand every sensible alternative to severe austerity as “nonsense,” they leave voters only one electable rebellion on offer, and the far right is happy to supply it. That is what is happening in France today.

proj-syn.title: Fukuyama, Thiel, and the Revenge of the Last Man
proj-syn.description: In his new memoir, Francis Fukuyama attempts to redeem his thesis about the end of history. But Peter Thiel’s ongoing quest to escape government oversight and wrest control of the future from democratic majorities makes a mockery of his argument all over again.

proj-syn.title: The Journalists’ Revolt Against AI Scraping
proj-syn.description: Big Tech’s oligopolistic dominance has prevented the news industry from developing a sustainable business model for the digital age—a crisis that AI is exacerbating. To preserve this important pillar of democracy, the Spanish-language publisher Editorial Perfil is suing OpenAI and Microsoft for copyright infringement.

proj-syn.title: MAGA’s Self-Destructive Culture War
proj-syn.description: Polls suggest that MAGA fanaticism might not be playing so well outside US President Donald Trump’s loyal base. But if the Democrats want to retake one or both chambers of Congress, they should concentrate on the economy and not answer Republican extremism with a culture war of their own.

proj-syn.title: How to Break the German Malaise
proj-syn.description: For too long, Germany’s political and corporate elite coasted on the country’s postwar economic and political success story, avoiding difficult but necessary reforms that could have kept extremist populist parties at bay. Now that the barbarians are at the gates, mainstream elites must rethink everything.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Place in the Global Redivision of Labor
proj-syn.description: While the US continues to lead in software, some high-tech sectors, and hydrocarbons, China is becoming increasingly competitive in many high-tech, capital-intensive sectors, not least those once dominated by Europe. The EU does have a relative advantage in this new economic order, if only its leaders would recognize it.

proj-syn.title: The World Has Passed Peak Trump
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump, previously the most powerful, unpredictable force on the international stage, has now passed the peak of his ability to disrupt the international order. With his approval ratings collapsing, foreign leaders whose tenures will extend beyond his own are starting to write him off.

proj-syn.title: Global Financial Reform that Centers African Women
proj-syn.description: While gender-equality objectives often fall by the wayside in times of upheaval, the current rupture in the multilateral order creates an opportunity to build a debt architecture that will deliver for the women of Africa. The first steps toward this goal can be taken at this month’s IMF–World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok.

proj-syn.title: How Africa Can Leverage the US-China Thaw
proj-syn.description: As dollar borrowing costs soar, Chinese rates are approaching record lows. This divergence, combined with the US-China thaw, creates an opportunity for African governments: partner with the US on gas and with China on solar and storage, and tap lower-cost Asian capital markets to finance investments in both.

proj-syn.title: Closing NATO’s Deterrence Gap
proj-syn.description: With Russian provocations against NATO member states growing more frequent, the alliance urgently needs to develop a credible doctrine of punitive deterrence to guide its response to acts of aggression that fall below the threshold of war. Mere territorial defense is not enough.

proj-syn.title: The India-Pakistan Cold War
proj-syn.description: The current stalemate between India and Pakistan should be viewed not as a pause between rounds of negotiation, but rather as part of a deliberate Indian strategy of disengagement. India will return to the negotiating table only after Pakistan dismantles, comprehensively and verifiably, its state-supported terrorist networks.

proj-syn.title: The Next Era of Reform Must Be About Capability
proj-syn.description: Economic development should no longer be measured solely by how much finance is mobilized or how much fiscal space is created. It must also be judged by whether countries emerge more capable of setting their own priorities, responding to challenges, and seizing new opportunities to shape their own future.

proj-syn.title: With AI, Sharing Is Caring
proj-syn.description: Although the public's distrust of Big Tech is understandable, given past experience, that is not a reason to starve AI models of the information and data they will need to be useful. If serving the public interest is the goal, everyone relying on the technology's output has a duty to provide high-quality input.

proj-syn.title: Why the US-China Trade Truce Matters
proj-syn.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump’s agreement to extend their trade truce reflects the fact that both sides have leverage over the other. In a world where the rules-based trading system is not functioning, the current fragile equilibrium may be the best one can hope for.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI And Energy Top A Busy Lineup Of Large Rounds
crunchbase.description: As the AI startup boom progresses, investors appear to be leaving few niches unfunded. That was apparent in this week’s lineup of large funding rounds, which featured AI infrastructure providers, a foundational model developer, a content protection platform for the AI age, and other AI-focused startups among the top investment recipients.

crunchbase.title: Active Investors Kept Up The Deal Pace In Q3, Even As Funding Fell
crunchbase.description: Active startup investors largely kept up or increased their dealmaking pace in the third quarter, even as overall venture funding declined with the absence of new record megarounds for AI leaders.

crunchbase.title: Why Customer Workflows Are Becoming The Moat In The AI Era
crunchbase.description: AI companies can build durable moats by embedding their products in essential customer workflows, explains tech adviser Itay Sagie, who shares why founders should prioritize measurable customer dependence, while investors and acquirers should assess how integrations, trusted relationships and workflow access can strengthen retention and drive growth.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: Gudea Lands $7M To Predict Which Online Narratives Will Go Viral
crunchbase.description: Gudea has raised $7 million in seed funding, co-led by Mudita Venture Partners and Silicon Road Ventures, to help companies anticipate which online narratives will go viral and understand who is driving them, the startup tells Crunchbase News exclusively.

crunchbase.title: Europe Posted Its Strongest Quarter In Q3 In 4 Years, As Its Venture Ecosystem Expands Beyond The UK
crunchbase.description: European startup funding reached $25 billion last quarter, well above the $14 billion invested in Q3 2025 and up slightly from the $24 billion invested in Q2. Quarterly funding was up 77% year over year, per Crunchbase data.

crunchbase.title: From Ballet To Breach Prevention: How A Magician’s Son Raised $4.2M In Seed Funding For His Cybersecurity Startup
crunchbase.description: The latest in our series of articles on venture funding to non-tech founders features a former magician's assistant and ballet dancer who's building cybersecurity software with $4.2 million in seed funding.

crunchbase.title: There Was Never An Easy AI Era, And Investors Are Raising The Bar
crunchbase.description: As AI IPOs bring greater scrutiny, argues guest author Maor Farid, founder and CEO of Leo AI, investors will increasingly prioritize customer spending growth, sustainable margins and deployment efficiency over rapid revenue growth alone.

crunchbase.title: North America’s Startup Funding Falls In Q3 As AI Giants Eye The Public Markets
crunchbase.description: In total, investors poured $92 billion into seed- through growth-stage rounds for U.S. and Canadian startups in the third quarter, per Crunchbase data. That’s a 35% decline from the prior quarter but up 50% from year-ago levels.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data Shows AI’s Most Active Startups Are Becoming Serial Acquirers
crunchbase.description: Some of the AI industry’s fastest-growing startups are becoming serial acquirers, buying smaller companies to fill product gaps, enter new markets and bring specialized teams in-house, a review of Crunchbase data shows. While AI giant OpenAI is by far the busiest of these buyers, well-funded startups in legal tech, customer service and software development have also made multiple acquisitions this year.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data: Q3 2026 Posted A Record Count Of Billion-Dollar Rounds As The Global AI Race Heats Up
crunchbase.description: Global venture funding totaled $159 billion in Q3 2026 with close to 6,000 startups funded, Crunchbase data shows. And while the third quarter was the lowest for startup investment so far this year, it still exceeded every other quarter since Q2 2022. We take a look at where the funding went.
